q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of an exhaust fan?
title: Exhaust fan carbon footprint per unit
short: Weigh the motor (copper winding and lamination steel), the blades and the plastic or metal frame per fan and multiply by supplier figures. Add winding, moulding, assembly and testing energy, then divide the unit's energy by fans passed.

ul: Copper winding wire and lamination steel for the motor.
Plastic or sheet metal frame and grille.
Stator winding and rotor die casting if done in-house.

p: Report per fan by sweep size, since a larger fan carries more motor and blade material.

example.title: Worked example: exhaust fan unit per unit (one month)
lines: Plant total: 17,750 / 20,000 = 0.887 kg CO2 per unit
Add copper, steel and plastic for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
